        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ steps.acceptance-artifact.outputs.name }}
          path: work
      - if: github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/')
        uses: ./
        with:
          operation: gate
          native-gate: 'true'
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-installation.outputs.assessment }}
          pull-request: ${{ needs.prepare-installation.outputs.number }}

      - if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: gate
          native-gate: 'true'
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-installation.outputs.assessment }}
          pull-request: ${{ needs.prepare-installation.outputs.number }}

  apply-repair:
    needs: [assess-intent, approve-and-merge, resolve-clouseau]
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      needs.assess-intent.result == 'success' && needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'failure' &&
      fromJSON(needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment).repair_digest != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: read
      actions: read
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '' }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: github.event_name != 'push'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Locate this run's acceptance record
        id: acceptance-artifact
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          retries: 3
          script: |
            const resolver = require(require('node:path').join(process.env.GITHUB_WORKSPACE, '.clouseau-ci/src/acceptance-artifact.cjs'));
            core.setOutput('name', await resolver.resolveArtifactName({github, context, attempt: process.env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT}));
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ steps.acceptance-artifact.outputs.name }}
          path: work
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: repair
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}
          repair-token: ${{ secrets.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}

  finalize-merge:
    needs: [assess-intent, approve-and-merge, resolve-clouseau]
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request_target'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '' }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: github.event_name != 'push'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: finalize
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  reconcile-base:
    # A sibling merge moves the base under every approved PR; nothing else re-checks them.
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    concurrency:
      group: clouseau-reconcile-base
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: reconcile-base
          update-token: ${{ secrets.BRANCH_UPDATE_TOKEN }}

  request-reassessment:
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/approve-intent ')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request != '' && !inputs.evaluate_acceptance)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    # issues and pull-requests write only for the notice that a requested reassessment could not be requested. Commenting on a
    # pull request with the workflow token needs both (issue 142: issues: write alone got HTTP 403). The job runs trusted main
    # and the frozen engine, never pull request code.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '' }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest || '' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: github.event_name != 'push'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: request-reassessment
          pull-request: ${{ inputs.pull_request }}

# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.
There is no application-specific deployment infrastructure in Clouseau.

## Operations

Automatic CI integrations reference the small `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`
bootstrap, so it always follows the latest protected main (the engine is resolved from protected
main at run time with the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the bootstrap adds little and
only goes stale). It selects protected Clouseau main,
freezes its SHA and computes its digest. Every engine job checks out that SHA
and invokes the local action with the same trusted outputs. Normal central
releases need no consumer pin or digest update; existing full-commit references keep working. See [automatic CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md)
for source authorization, failure behavior and exact local-receipt compatibility.
Legacy fixed installations may still use `gaulatti/clouseau@FULL_REVIEWED_COMMIT_SHA`;
upgrading those installations requires a reviewed PR. See `examples/colombo.json`
for the version 2 policy configuration.

| `coverage` | Accepted-base v2 `coverage-config`, or legacy `coverage-report` + `source-directory` with optional `coverage-format` | Require exact, nonempty 100% native application line and branch coverage; the two input forms are mutually exclusive. A repository can opt in to [changed-line coverage](docs/changed-line-coverage.md) with `coverage.mode` in its protected config plus `coverage-base-ref` and `coverage-baseline`, or in [declared coverage](docs/declared-coverage.md) (`"declared"`: enforce the minimums the client's `package.json` declares at the base revision; needs `coverage-base-ref` only) |

The wait is cheap and rate-limit aware: a running verification is polled every 15 s, an absent or queued one at growing gaps (15, 30, 60, then 120 s; about 10 requests for the default grace instead of 60), and the workflow-run listing is a conditional request (`If-None-Match`; a 304 does not count against the primary limit). A 403/429 (retry-after, `x-ratelimit-remaining`/`reset`, secondary or abuse limit) is retried with bounded exponential backoff and jitter that respects the stated reset. If the budget stays exhausted past the bounded wait, the review ends in an explicit hold, `Held: GitHub API rate limit, will retry after <time>`, shown in the `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment (`github_rate_limit`) and in the `retry_after` output; the next verification completion or a re-run after that time reassesses the PR.

For example, a caller's coverage step supplies:

```yaml
with:
  operation: coverage
  coverage-report: coverage.json
  source-directory: src
```

The report must contain every compiled application path, including uncovered
code. Vendor/dependency coverage cannot mask application gaps. Counts must match
exactly; rounded percentages, missing data, or a zero branch total fail. The
caller owns instrumentation and test execution. Colombo uses Rust nightly branch
instrumentation with normal application cfgs, followed by docs and Docker tests.

For JavaScript/TypeScript, select `coverage-format: istanbul` and pass the native
`coverage-final.json` produced by c8/Istanbul. Set `source-directory` to the
original application source tree, not compiled output. Every `.ts`, `.tsx`,
`.js`, `.jsx`, `.cjs`, and `.mjs` source must appear, including unloaded modules.
Declaration-only `.d.ts` files, concrete test conventions and dependency
directories are not application sources; generated application code remains
included. The fixed inventory conventions and multi-artifact configuration are
documented in [local coverage plans](docs/local-review.md#multiple-native-coverage-artifacts).
The checker rejects omitted,
duplicate, mismatched, skipped or malformed measurements and coverage-ignore
directives. Empty statement maps require a parse-only source check: missing
native statement-counter sites are rejected, while genuine statement-free
declarations remain valid. Branch-only declarations still require native branch
measurements. This check needs Node.js and uses the declared, bundled parser;
it never executes application source or loads application Babel configuration.
It derives exact line and branch totals from native hit counters,
never from rounded summary percentages. Configure c8 `--all` over all compiled
JavaScript with source maps to measure unloaded TypeScript sources. Run real
runtime tests as well as unit tests; this format support does not replace them.
See [native empty-map validation](docs/istanbul-source-validation.md) for its
producer trust boundary, runtime dependency and parser provenance.

For Python, select `coverage-format: coveragepy` and supply the unmodified JSON
format 3 report from `coverage.py` with branch measurement enabled. See the
[native Python coverage contract](docs/python-coverage.md) for source inventory,
report generation, path binding and exact native counter validation. This reads
coverage.py's executable lines and branch decision exits, not statement
percentages or every traced transition. Empty global totals, omitted application
modules, exclusions, partial coverage and inconsistent counters fail closed.

For Go, select `coverage-format: go` and supply the `go test -coverprofile` text
profile built with `-coverpkg=./...`. Go records statements and basic blocks only, so
`lines` means statements and `branches` means basic blocks; implicit false exits and
short-circuit operands are not measured. See the [native Go coverage
contract](docs/go-coverage.md) for exact semantics, inventory and failures.

For Swift, produce LCOV with `swift test --enable-code-coverage` and `xcrun llvm-cov export -format=lcov`
and declare `source_suffixes: [".swift"]` on an `lcov` part. The toolchain records no branch outcomes, so a
pure Swift part fails the exact gate with `No branches measured`; see the [Swift coverage
recipe](docs/swift-coverage.md).

Monorepos may use the accepted-base version 2 local recipe with separate native
Istanbul, coverage.py and Go parts. `operation: coverage` accepts that recipe through
`coverage-config` and uses the shared per-part and aggregate measurement rules.
The CI gate requires each part to be complete and exact; local AI can assess
honest partial or unavailable measurements. There is no consumer-side report
merging. Legacy single-report inputs remain supported.

## Trust and permissions

Keep test execution and privileged review in separate jobs. Contributor code runs
on disposable read-only PR runners with no secrets. Assessment and gating must
check out only the protected base branch; configuration, README, and repository
contract files are read from that trusted checkout. PR patches, source, commit
messages, and tickets are untrusted evidence and never executed by the reviewer.

The `assess` job needs actions/contents/pull-requests/issues read permissions and
the repository's `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. `gate` needs contents/pull-requests/issues/
actions write permissions and must receive no provider key. Pass the
assessment output between jobs. The action cannot elevate the caller's token.
Version 1's shared model is `deepseek-flash`; changes are sent to it only after
technical verification succeeds. It assesses repository fit and supported intent,
including large test improvements. There is no file-count or line-count approval
cutoff. New product decisions and unclear scope require the owner’s judgment.
A missing or token-truncated provider completion is retried within the same
read-only assessment, using the identical evidence, at most three attempts total.
Retries wait one then two seconds. The output budget starts at 4,096 tokens and
doubles only after a token-limit truncation, capped at 16,384 tokens per request.
Every request retains its 90-second timeout. Fixed attempt/outcome/token-budget
categories are logged without model text, reasoning, patches, or credentials.
A complete verdict stops retries immediately, including second opinions,
integrity rejections, and invalid or wrong-revision evidence. HTTP failures,
network/decoding errors, unknown terminal finish reasons, and exhausted retries
fail closed and require a second opinion. The provider health probe is unchanged. AI must also support test integrity with evidence about assertions
and failure cases. Detected test fakery blocks approval, including after an intent
confirmation. Coverage percentages alone cannot satisfy that assessment. No numerical confidence score grants approval.

`sensitive_paths` lists additional paths the consumer explicitly protects with
owner confirmation. The example leaves it empty; ordinary test, dependency,
and infrastructure paths are assessed by AI rather than rejected by filename.
The configured verification workflow, review controls, and repository-purpose
contract remain protected. Their changes still receive an AI integrity assessment
and require explicit owner confirmation.

`managed_agents` is an opt-in, default-off exception for one protected path: an
`AGENTS.md` change whose managed block is byte-identical to a digest enrolled in the
protected configuration, with every byte outside the block unchanged, is not held for
owner confirmation. See [managed-standard AGENTS.md updates](docs/managed-agents.md).

`exact_revert` is an opt-in, default-off exception for one review: a PR whose resulting tree is
byte-identical to an earlier first-parent tree of the base history, within a window set in the protected
configuration, is accepted without a fresh AI review; protected controls still need the exact-head owner
confirmation and verification is unchanged. See [exact revert acceptance](docs/exact-revert.md).

The native protected merge path requires active effective base-branch rules: strict required
checks for the configured verification job and native `approve-and-merge` job
from GitHub Actions, a fresh approving review, no deletion, and no force pushes. The installing
administrator must also verify no bypass actors. Repository auto-merge and Actions
approving reviews must be enabled for automatic merge. Runtime tokens do not get administration access.

Missing or insufficient repository settings are a notice, never a failure. The review, acceptance
record and approval complete and the job succeeds, but Clouseau neither arms nor performs the
merge. It posts one fixed-text comment, updated in place, naming only bounded classes: auto-merge
disabled, main not protected, required checks missing, approval freshness missing, up-to-date
missing, force-push+deletion protection missing. Security reasoning: without protection the bot
approval cannot make an unsafe merge more possible than it already is, so it is harmless, while
merging or arming auto-merge on insufficient protection stays forbidden. API errors other than a
reported gap still fail.

Protocol v2 also supports explicit `"merge_mode": "manual"` in accepted base
configuration. Repository auto-merge must be disabled in this mode, including
for owner-authored PRs. Tests, exact coverage, review, source binding and
current-head code-owner approval for external contributors when CODEOWNERS is configured remain mandatory.
Available branch protection is still enforced. Only GitHub's specific HTTP 403
private-plan upgrade response, together with verified private visibility and an
unprotected branch, permits approval without host-enforced protection. Generic
permission failures, unavailable APIs, public unprotected repositories and
incomplete available rules fail closed. The summary states when GitHub cannot
enforce the checks; trusted maintainers must honor them before manually merging.
The controller never merges or dispatches deployment in manual mode.

This repository explicitly selects `"merge_mode": "automatic"` for strict owner-only automation:
CODEOWNERS must exist on the accepted base and the author must own every affected
path. The normal protected native flow is unchanged. On the exact unavailable
private-plan condition above, native repository auto-merge stays disabled while
the validated acceptance controller can atomically fast-forward the exact base
to the reviewed head, with paired source/base compare-and-swap and no force.
This supports same-repository branches with an up-to-date head only; other
contributions remain manual. Missing/stale reviews, failed full verification or
coverage, changed revisions and API errors cannot authorize that write. This is
controller-enforced delivery, not unavailable native branch protection. See
[the complete private-plan contract](docs/change-acceptance.md#controller-enforced-owner-merge-on-an-unavailable-private-plan),
including deployment-trigger limitations. Omitting `merge_mode` preserves the
existing native flow and optional CODEOWNERS behavior.

Manual decisions assign the PR to `manual_reviewer` and request that person's
review. Owner-authored PRs use assignment without an invalid self-review request.
The owner can comment `/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA`; this confirms intent only.
An owner confirmation can carry the actual accepted requirement, rather than
leaving investigators to infer it from a revision alone:

```text
/approve-intent FULL_HEAD_SHA

Accepted purpose:
Describe the accepted outcome and its boundaries.
```

Clouseau authenticates the configured owner and current permission, binds the
literal requirement to that revision and revalidates it before writing. Ordinary
PR prose remains untrusted; every mechanism still earns its own justification.
An agent delegated to install an accepted scope may record these confirmations
on the owner's behalf through its repairs without repeated approval prompts.
All tests and exact coverage remain mandatory. Changes invalidate the decision.
The Actions bot cannot approve its own PR; it needs an independent human review.
First-time fork workflow authorization remains GitHub's responsibility.

The PR report starts with a plain-language decision, one conservative scorecard,
and one entry per causal technical finding. Each entry shows its consequence,
blocking score, affected area, evidence and required outcome. Reviewer
disagreements, product rework, missing evidence and owner decisions stay visible.
The lowest product scores across all material changes and both reviewers are
shown; unrelated good scores never compensate for a failing change. Optional
findings show expected benefit and optional priority without creating a blocker.

Expand **Scoring and evidence** for the unchanged formulas, every individual
grade and explanation, both independent reviews, persistent finding history and
the evidence register (source and line ranges). Source text is not copied into PR
comments; the complete source-bound record stays in the run's acceptance artifact.
Large audits retain lossless evidence pages. Summary
formatting uses the already validated record and makes no model requests. A
review decision never claims that merge, deployment or live verification finished.

The display regression includes the actual public Palazzo #27 review, linked to
its immutable signed evidence. Its original comment contains 36,564 characters;
5,388 remain visible with evidence sections closed. The new overview contains
948 visible characters, over five times shorter, with the same approved
verdict, both reviewers' 100/100 product scores and no technical findings. This
is an offline display fixture, never a substitute for fresh review or CI evidence.

Version 2 additionally uploads `work/clouseau-acceptance*.json` as a run/attempt
bound artifact (`clouseau-acceptance-<run id>-<attempt>`) and downloads it into
`work/` in the separate approval and repair jobs. The download resolves the
artifact by run id with `src/acceptance-artifact.cjs` (a `actions/github-script`
step named `Locate this run's acceptance record`, see this repository's
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`), taking the newest attempt that is not later than the
current one, because `gh run rerun --failed` re-runs only the failed approval job
as a new attempt while the successful assessment job's artifact keeps its
original attempt number. The lookup accepts only artifacts of this run id and
this revision of the workflow that have not expired; the gate still compares
the record against the assessment's digests, head, base and frozen engine.
**A consumer that copied the artifact-transport workflow must update its copy**
(add the lookup step after the engine checkout and download the name it outputs)
before a failed-jobs re-run can find the assessment; `record-transport:
job-output` consumers need only the engine update. Once the review is accepted
the merge step is safe to repeat: enabling auto-merge and submitting the approval
retry transient GitHub failures (GraphQL "Something went wrong", HTTP 5xx and
short secondary rate limits) after 2, 6 and 15 s. Validation, permission and
"not mergeable" errors fail at once with GitHub's message. If the transient
failure persists the job fails with a notice that the review was already
accepted and that re-running the failed job is safe and repeats no AI review. Select examiner, challenger and grader explicitly in `acceptance`; see
[the self-hosting configuration](.github/clouseau.json). `typesafe-key` is needed
only when the explicit Jev/DeepSeek grading route is selected. Failure never
silently changes that choice. A separate repair job receives an independent
author token through `repair-token`; Colombo reuses its existing deployment
token. Neither the approval job nor AI inspection receives that author token. The repair
job requires a trusted GitHub head repository matching the base repository before
loading the author credential; the writer independently rechecks that identity.
Only purpose/authority decisions can use owner confirmation in version 2.

The consumer must retain PR, metadata-only target, comment, and manual workflow
entry points and PR-level concurrency. The controller validates the exact latest
PR-event run, revision, verification job, and named steps from configuration.
The read-only `assess` job waits for the PR verification run to finish before
calling AI. That wait occupies a runner, and a verification job that is queued
behind it on a single-slot pool can never start, so the wait is bounded by
progress (see "Waiting for verification" in `docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md`). Allow 70 minutes for this job when verification can take 60 minutes.
The separate native job named `approve-and-merge` calls `gate`; it must run on
`pull_request_target` and fail if assessment fails, intent is missing, integrity
is rejected, or technical evidence is incomplete. Use `always()` with `needs`
so a failed assessment cannot silently skip the required gate. In other event
contexts, use a different job name to avoid a skipped duplicate required check.
The `native-gate` and `wait-for-verification` action inputs default to `true`.

The native job summary preserves detailed reasons; no additional API check is
created in native mode. A `GITHUB_TOKEN` API check can attach to another run's
suite and is insufficient as the required approval result for this flow. Comment/manual handlers call
`request-reassessment` with actions write, contents read, and issues and pull-requests
write access; they rerun the current revision's existing `pull_request_target` run. Its test job
is skipped, so confirming intent does not rebuild the container. The handler
validates maintainer permission and exact comment SHA before requesting a rerun.
A request that does not validate is refused, not ignored. That covers an `/approve-intent` or `/hosted-review` naming

never reads the confirmation into a decision itself: only a new assessment does.

write and contents/pull-requests read access and no provider key. Guard that job
on the gate's explicit result (`!cancelled() && needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'success'`),

bake windows, and ticket closure remain separate delivery work.

```sh

```

all production JavaScript modules. New source files are included
even when no test imports them. Test code is outside the production scope;
there are no exclusions for production failure paths or rounded thresholds.

under real coverage.py to prove the `coveragepy` adapter against live output, so
install `requirements-test.txt` (coverage.py 7.13.0) to run the whole suite. The

CI also exercises the packaged composite action and verifies both passing and

The new repository's wiki is not initialized; operational documentation lives
here until a wiki is available.

The `evaluate-review` operation calls the real provider with three committed
synthetic review contexts. Maintenance must qualify, unrelated product scope
must request an owner decision, and test-specific validation bypasses must block
approval. A wrong or unavailable decision fails the evaluation. The GitHub and
technical-readiness inputs are fixtures; these evaluations validate model judgment,
not actual test execution or an end-to-end PR merge. The maintenance case injects
one synthetic truncated completion before calling the real provider to verify
automatic recovery within the same assessment. Logs identify that injection
explicitly; it is not evidence of a naturally occurring provider outage. Controller regression tests
use simulated provider decisions separately. Run live evaluations only in a
read-only diagnostic job with the provider key and no repository write token.

exact deployment source revision and current wiki. A read-only job plans the
complete page set, generates each page against that common plan, validates links
and navigation, and independently fact-checks every proposed page, including
retained claims. Existing wiki prose can be stale; production control flow takes
precedence. The full bundle must pass before it becomes a publishable artifact.

DeepSeek V4 Pro with low reasoning effort; Flash uses non-thinking mode at
temperature zero. DeepSeek's
[beta strict function-return format](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/tool_calls/)
provides separate schemas for planning, the exact requested page, and factual
review. The sole return name is `wiki_result`. Its arguments are parsed as data;
no model-selected function is executed. Plain-text answers, unknown return names,
multiple returns, and incomplete results fail closed. The factual checker uses
automatic tool choice because the provider forbids forced choices in thinking
mode; a plain answer still fails validation. Token truncation retries
use identical evidence and schemas, at most three attempts with 4,096/8,192/16,384
output tokens and 90-second deadlines. PR review keeps its existing API and
reasoning policy.

Each page receives a dedicated factual audit with the complete source map and
the other proposed pages for consistency. The combined factual report is a fixed
checklist keyed by the planned pages. Each page
has one source reference, a findings string limited to 2,000 characters, and a
supported verdict emitted last. Every page must be supported with no unresolved
findings; contradictory verdicts are rejected. This avoids unbounded evidence
arrays while retaining an independent judgment for every updated page.

Source references select controller-assigned `path:Lnumber` IDs. The native
response schema restricts paths to actual source filenames; shortened basenames
are not accepted. The source map preserves exact lines, including blanks.
Local validation rejects invented IDs, blank citations, and missing page checks.
The model cannot substitute quotation text.
This is an AI quality gate rather than a proof of semantic correctness;
documentation still needs correction when new evidence reveals an error.

A rejected factual draft may receive up to three correction passes from actionable findings.
Only pages with findings are regenerated; other page bytes are preserved. The
complete corrected batch must differ, pass structural/link validation again,
and receive a fresh supporting factual verdict. No previously rejected text is
resubmitted, including cycles between drafts. Missing findings or an exhausted
correction budget stops publication. The
read-only `evaluate-wiki` operation disables correction and calls the real model
on supported authentication and shared-refresh documents plus deliberate
denial/unavailability and FTP-only-refresh falsehoods. Provider, schema, or citation failures cannot count as a successful
negative result.

Live evaluation case diagnostics are saved at `wiki-plan.json.evaluation.json`,
including when a positive or negative control fails. Structured generation
diagnostics are saved beside the plan at
`wiki-plan.json.diagnostic.json`. Rejected planning values are retained before
any generation. Factual diagnostics contain each reviewed draft, findings, and
its immutable source-line map. Consumers should upload diagnostics even when
planning fails. No provider credentials or raw transport bodies are stored.

A separate publisher receives no model key or deployment credentials. It downloads
only its own workflow run's artifact and independently verifies the repository,
source SHA, wiki base SHA, run ID, and the expected main workflow's completed
successful deployment job. Draft generation can skip deployment verification;
publication never can. Generation needs `actions: read` and `contents: read`.
Only publication needs `contents: write` and a Git-authenticated wiki checkout.

Consumer `.github/clouseau-wiki.json` specifies every field explicitly:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "source_paths": ["README.md", "src/", "migrations/", "Dockerfile", "compose.yaml", "Makefile", "scripts/", ".env.example", ".github/workflows/"],
  "deployment_workflow": "backend-deploy.yml",
  "deployment_job": "deploy",
  "wiki_branch": "master"
}
```

Only committed text in those paths is read. Real `.env` files and agent-rule paths
are refused; wiki agent instructions are excluded from model context. The wiki
must be a clean, initialized Git checkout. Pages are flat Markdown filenames,
including Home, `_Sidebar`, and `_Footer`; the model cannot change configuration,
edit `AGENTS.md`, or delete pages. Local limits are twenty pages, 128,000 bytes per
page, 512,000 bytes per bundle, 300 source files, and 1,000,000 bytes per complete
request. Nothing is silently truncated. Unsafe paths, duplicate/ambiguous names,
broken internal links, orphaned new pages, unsupported link syntax, and unclosed
code fences fail validation.

Publication uses a private temporary Git index, never model-directed filesystem
writes. All pages and the `.clouseau-deployment.json` source/run receipt form one
commit. A changed remote wiki base or rejected non-force push publishes nothing;
concurrent human edits are never rebased or overwritten. A repeated source SHA
is idempotent. A new revision with no Markdown changes records a truthful audit
receipt. Serialize deployment and documentation together to prevent a later
release from overtaking documentation. Documentation failure leaves the completed
deployment intact and makes the workflow fail visibly; it does not roll back or
claim external service health, running image bytes, or terminal upload delivery.

Reviews retain fixed/dismissed findings across pushes and explicitly inventory
inspected, excluded and missing evidence. Missing material context prevents
approval. When protected-base CODEOWNERS exists, protocol v2 enables automatic merge only for code-owner-authored PRs;
other contributions require current-head code-owner approval and manual merge.
Confirmed absence leaves that ownership gate inactive; existing invalid files or
unavailable ownership evidence still block. Other acceptance gates are unchanged.
See [the review contract](docs/change-acceptance.md#review-convergence-and-completeness).

The frozen qualification corpus in `test/acceptance-cases.cjs` includes clean
maintenance, a real executable zero-body regression, product drift, unnecessary
machinery, deceptive tests, a dismissed false allegation and unavailable material
context. Each case has an expected disposition and an evidence-based rationale.
A blocking verdict on an unrelated issue does not qualify the known-defect case.

`node test/evaluate-acceptance.cjs` performs live judgment qualification using the

Completed negative decisions are retained, never retried to seek approval. Only unusable

Recorded-response tests exercise transport parsing, validation, history and
scoring without calling a model. They are deterministic software evidence,
not evidence of a replacement model's review quality. Provider changes require
a complete live corpus qualification against the same frozen inputs and expected
outcomes; no provider is switched automatically by these tests. Replay is allowed
only for unchanged source/policy/routing inputs and is labeled separately from
new live calls. Qualification fixtures do not establish a genuine PR merge.

# Automatic CI upgrades

Clouseau's protected review workflow uses the shared protocol below. Palazzo
and Colombo enable it through their own protected workflow installation PRs;
the shared release alone does not install consumer CI.
“Latest” means the commit returned for `gaulatti/clouseau`'s protected `main`
when the workflow's isolated `resolve-clouseau` job starts. It does not mean a
release tag, a contributor branch, or an unmerged candidate. Protection and the
central review process authorize that source; signatures retain their existing
workstation trust boundary.

The small `scripts/resolve` bootstrap is referenced in trusted consumer workflow
configuration as `gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main`, never a commit pin, tag, other
branch or fork. The engine itself is resolved from protected main at run time and runs with
the repository's secrets, so a commit pin on the small bootstrap adds little protection and
only creates stale pins; following main also means a bootstrap maintenance change reaches
consumers without an installation PR. An existing full-commit reference keeps working, but
new installations use `@main`. It has no source-selection inputs. It checks the public GitHub
branch response, requires protected main and a full lowercase commit SHA, checks
out that SHA without persisted credentials, and computes the engine content
digest from that actual source. Unavailable, malformed and unprotected results
fail the workflow. There is no previous-version fallback or private dependency.

Every engine job directly needs that resolver and checks out its SHA. Jobs pass
`CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA` and `CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST` from those job outputs; the
local action verifies the actual content and, when available, checkout commit.
Bootstrap identification checks the clean revision both before and after hashing.
These are trusted workflow values, never PR text or uploaded evidence. Git-free
action bundles verify their content digest against the same immutable selection.
Missing resolver output selects an invalid all-zero commit at checkout, so it
cannot silently select a default branch. The required approval job also fails
when resolution prevents assessment.
Tests of Clouseau itself still exercise proposed code; ordinary protected review
uses central main. The existing explicit owner-authorized installation path is
separate from automatic source selection. Explicit controller-installation pushes
skip the automatic resolver and use only their guarded, frozen candidate. They
do not publish an unused protected-main selection as their engine evidence.

GitHub action `uses` references cannot select a revision from runtime outputs.
Use a literal local action path after `actions/checkout` with an expression in
`with.ref`. Do not resolve main independently in each job. See GitHub's
[workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idstepsuses)
and [context availability](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#context-availability).

Assessment outputs and acceptance artifacts bind the frozen SHA and computed
digest. Approval, score recalculation, repairs and finalization verify the same
identity. Advancing central main cannot change an already selected run; the next
run selects the new approved commit. Rerunning the resolver job makes a new
selection, so rerun the whole workflow after a release rather than combining
old successful jobs with a new selection.

## Consumer verify jobs need no provider secret

A consumer's `.github/tests/provider-recovery.test.mjs` (a consumer-owned file)
imports `src/provider.cjs` from the frozen `.clouseau-ci` checkout and calls
`requestReview` with an injected `fetchImpl`. Because the checkout is the
resolved engine revision, an engine fix reaches every installed consumer with no
consumer change; consumers do not carry a copy of the provider.

`requestReview` therefore does not validate `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` itself. The
named, secret-free notice for a missing or malformed key comes from
`policy.assess` (and `requestJSON` / `requestWiki` / `checkProvider` for their own
paths), which run before any request in a real review. A `verify` job, a fork PR
or a fresh installation with no provider secret must pass. Engine revisions
`d0d773b` through `bc88519` regressed this; fixed revisions need no consumer
edit. If a consumer ever pins an affected revision, the minimal workaround is
`process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ??= 'fictional-test-key';` at the top of the test,
and the upgrade path is to advance to the fixed `main`.

## Receipt route fallback upgrade

The reference `examples/consumer-ci.yml` sends a PR whose description carries a
`clouseau-local-review` marker to a receipt-only `verify-local` step that holds no provider
secret. Before this change an unusable receipt there ended `review_incomplete` and the owner had to
delete the marker by hand. The reference now continues in the same run with an `assess-hosted`
job. A consumer carries a copy of the workflow, so a consumer that wants the behavior applies
these edits (a normal reviewed workflow PR; workflow files are protected controls and need the
exact-head `/approve-intent`). The copy keeps working unchanged without them.

1. `assess-intent`: add the job output `hosted: ${{ steps.fallback.outputs.hosted }}` and the step
   `fallback` after the `local-review` step (`if: steps.review-route.outputs.local == 'true'`, a
   `github-script` that sets `hosted` to `'true'` only when the parsed assessment has decision
   `review_incomplete` and cause `local_receipt_unusable`).
2. Add the `assess-hosted` job exactly as in the reference: `needs: [assess-intent, resolve-clouseau]`,
   `if: needs.assess-intent.outputs.hosted == 'true'`, a checkout of `main`, the frozen engine, and one
   `assess` step with `ignore-receipt: 'true'`, `record-transport: job-output`,
   `pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}` and the provider keys. It must read no other
   output of `assess-intent`.
3. `approve-and-merge`, `apply-repair` and `finalize-merge`: add `assess-hosted` to `needs`, and replace every
   `needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment` / `.review-record` with
   `needs.assess-hosted.outputs.<name> || needs.assess-intent.outputs.<name>` so one record is consumed
   per head. Extend the "Require a completed assessment" guard with
   `contains(fromJSON('["failure","cancelled"]'), needs.assess-hosted.result)` and let `apply-repair` accept a
   skipped hosted job (`contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), needs.assess-hosted.result)`).
   Give `finalize-merge` an explicit guard,
   `!cancelled() && needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'success' && (<the review-event condition>)`: a valid
   receipt skips `assess-hosted`, and a job whose `if` calls no status function is skipped with any skipped
   need, so `if: *review-event` alone never finalizes or dispatches deployment for a receipt-merged PR.
4. Pin the engine to a revision that includes the `ignore-receipt` input before adding the job. GitHub only
   warns about an unknown input, so an older engine would silently read the receipt in the secret-bearing job.
   Rollback is reverting the workflow PR.

`.github/tests/receipt-fallback.test.mjs` encodes this template.

## Repository-local receipt authorization

Keep signer enrollment, author binding, maximum age and revocation in protected
base configuration. Replace the recurring `local_review.reviewer_digest` field
with:

```json
"central_source": {"repository": "gaulatti/clouseau", "ref": "refs/heads/main"}
```

The two configuration modes are exclusive. During the owner-confirmed
installation transition, a frozen central identity supplied by trusted workflow
configuration can authorize the engine while protected signer configuration
still contains its legacy digest. Without that trusted run identity, the legacy
digest remains mandatory. A receipt never supplies that authorization. Proposed PR configuration cannot
enroll a source or signer. CI checks the receipt's exact engine SHA and digest
against its frozen, checked-out source. A receipt cannot supply its own accepted
digest. No version-label or implicit cross-version compatibility is supported.

A matching eligible signature reuses the independent local review with zero CI
AI calls. Independent tests, exact 100% line and branch coverage, current source,
base, policy and configuration checks remain mandatory. Review-control changes require a separate, current-head owner purpose
confirmation. The receipt supplies the scored review only; CI records and
revalidates that separate authorization before approval. Missing receipts in optional mode use
the ordinary CI AI reviewer. So does any receipt that does not verify in every
respect (malformed, unknown or revoked key, bad signature, wrong author, expired,
wrong head or base, changed policy, configuration or record, different engine
revision, changed sources or diff, or a review that did not pass): it is ignored,
never accepted as evidence, CI performs every check itself and the PR shows one
fixed notice naming a bounded reason class. An ignored receipt cannot approve
anything. In `required` mode there is no hosted review, so the outcome is
`local_receipt_required` with the same notice. Refresh the public
local installation, review the current committed source again, publish a fresh
receipt, and start a fresh CI run to reuse the local review. A central advance during that interval may
require another fresh review; previous evidence must remain available.

Local investigators can inspect `.clouseau-ci/` source requests through their
own frozen public engine. This alias requires no consumer CI checkout and
adds no authority to the source. Signed engine excerpts carry the exact engine
revision; CI compares their bytes to its accepted frozen source before reuse.
The bootstrap is part of the seed (`.clouseau-ci/scripts/resolve/action.yml`) for a workflow that
follows main; a workflow that still carries a full-commit reference can also have that historical
bootstrap inspected as `.clouseau-ci/scripts/resolve/action.yml@FULL_COMMIT_SHA`. Historical source is
read-only untrusted evidence from the fixed public Clouseau repository; it never
selects or executes a different review engine. CI verifies its exact immutable
bytes. Changed resolver workflows receive at most 32 observed shared source/test
dependencies up front, including their actual bootstrap and the legacy
action/configuration/policy/receipt files read during migration. Wiki dependencies
are included only when the changed workflow invokes them. Changed project files
and contracts are still complete. Serialized evidence remains capped at 900,000
characters, as enforced by the existing collector. Changed dependency lockfiles
count as a bounded derived summary, not as raw text (see
`docs/change-acceptance.md`). Incomplete local reviews
retain the delivered snapshot and journal,
and the error identifies their private local evidence directory.
The final allowed local source batch is delivered before the report turn; it is
not read and discarded at the investigation limit. Eight local batches of up to
eight
paths are the maximum. The larger bounded allowance addresses the actual
multi-repository installation investigation, which needed more than three
batches within the existing source-size ceiling. Another source request still
fails closed.

Local-only installations still need only the public Clouseau source and an
authenticated coding harness. CI configuration and provider credentials are not
installed by bastille startup. The signature authenticates an enrolled
workstation's evidence; it does not defend against a compromised workstation.

## Waiting for verification

The `pull_request_target` review run and the `pull_request` verification run are
different workflow runs, so `needs:` cannot order them. A review job that polls
for verification therefore holds a runner while it waits. On a runner pool with
one slot the queued `Verify PR` job can never start behind it, and the review
used to sit until its deadline (about 30 minutes) and fail without a decision.

The review no longer holds a runner indefinitely, and no manual rerun is needed:

1. Use the `await-verification` operation instead of an inline polling script
   (`assess` with the default `wait-for-verification` applies the same rule).
   While the exact-head verification run is `in_progress` the job keeps polling.
   If no run exists or it is still queued longer than the **queue grace**, the
   step ends cleanly with output `verified=false`, makes no decision and
   creates no acceptance record. Later assessment steps are skipped with
   `if: steps.<id>.outputs.verified == 'true'`. A failed or changed verification
   still fails the step.
2. `approve-and-merge` stays red (fail closed): a record-less run cannot approve
   or merge, and its message is the run's own reason ("Waiting for
   verification..."), never a missing protocol-two record.
3. When the PR verification run completes, a `workflow_run` trigger starts the
   `request-reassessment` operation, which reruns the exact-head
   `pull_request_target` run (waiting for it to finish if it is still ending)
   unless that run already succeeded. The rerun finds verification complete and
   produces the record. Contributor tests are not rerun.

Configure the grace in `.github/clouseau.json` (whole seconds, 0 to 3600,
default 900):

```json
"verification_queue_grace_seconds": 900
```

The default is conservative so a slow runner pool is not mistaken for a
deadlock. A single-slot pool never needs the whole grace; lower it (for example
60) to release the slot sooner. With a larger pool nothing changes while
verification is running or starting within the grace.

Consumer workflow template (names are the consumer's own). The reassessment trigger lives in a
**separate workflow file** that watches the verification workflow: GitHub does not start a workflow from
its own completion, so a `workflow_run` trigger that names the workflow containing it never fires.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (the verification workflow, named "Palazzo CI")
on:
  pull_request:
  pull_request_target:
jobs:
  assess-intent:
    outputs:
      # the wait step publishes a precise incomplete assessment if verification truly failed, so the
      # write-capable job can post the visible notice
      assessment: ${{ steps.assess.outputs.assessment || steps.wait.outputs.assessment }}
    steps:
      # checkout main, then the frozen engine into .clouseau-ci, as for assess
      - id: wait
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: await-verification
      - id: assess
        if: steps.wait.outputs.verified == 'true'
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: assess   # or verify-local
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/clouseau-reassess.yml (a different file)
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Palazzo CI"]      # the verification workflow's name, never this workflow's own
    types: [completed]
jobs:
  request-reassessment:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'
    permissions: {contents: read, pull-requests: read, actions: write}
    # checkout main and the frozen engine, then operation: request-reassessment
```

The `workflow_run` event is a trusted run of the watched workflow, so it needs no
maintainer comment; the engine accepts only a `pull_request` run of the
configured workflow whose head is still the ready PR's head. The shared contract
tests `assertBoundedVerificationWait` (no inline `technicalRun` polling; later
steps gated on `verified`) and `assertReassessmentOnVerification` (the trigger
and job exist, and the trigger watches a different workflow than the one
containing it) encode this template. Where verification starts promptly the
review never ends pending and the trigger finds the run already succeeded.

The verification wait decides only from the final state of the latest attempt of the
exact-head `pull_request` run. A completed run whose job or step list is still being
finalized (jobs in progress, steps without a conclusion, an empty list, a job list from a newer
attempt than the run record) is re-read a bounded number of times and otherwise stays pending;
it is never converted into a failure. A final failure names the run, job or step
(`Required verification step "..." concluded skipped`) in an incomplete assessment that
`await-verification` publishes through the composite action's `assessment` output (it
maps `steps.assess` or, for this operation, `steps.await`). The wait step then ends
cleanly with `verified=false`: it does not fail, so the `assess-intent` job succeeds, hands
the assessment to `approve-and-merge` through the job output
`steps.assess.outputs.assessment || steps.wait.outputs.assessment`, and the gate posts the
visible `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment naming the failed step and then holds (it
cannot approve or merge). A consumer that does not list the wait step's output in the job
output gets no notice; `assertBoundedVerificationWait` rejects that.

Every other way the wait can end without a green verification is also visible. `await-verification`
publishes the same kind of assessment, so the gate posts a comment and holds: a verification still
queued or running when the queue grace (default 900 s, measured in waited time, not polls) or the
wait budget ends is `pending_technical`, shown as one short, idempotent `clouseau-review-pending`
comment ("waiting for PR verification; the review runs again automatically when it completes",
replaced by a resolution line once a decision exists); an exhausted GitHub API budget is
`review_incomplete` with cause `github_rate_limit` and the retry time. The wait does not end early:
a review that ended after about two minutes with no comment had been stopped by a rate-limit hold
(the budget is shared by every open PR), not by the grace. The reassessment trigger uses the same
bounded backoff; if the budget is still exhausted it fails with `Reassessment held: ... Re-run this
job after that time`, never an unhandled HttpError.

Any other HTTP error from GitHub during the wait also ends visibly: the wait publishes a
`review_incomplete` assessment with cause `github_api_error` and the reason
`GitHub API request failed: HTTP <status> <method> <owner>/<repo>/<path> (<message>)` (no host, query
or credential), which the gate posts as the `clouseau-review-incomplete` comment. A PR read that GitHub
refuses with "too many files changed" (a small PR on a branch far behind a busy base: GitHub cannot
compute the diff statistics for `GET /pulls/{n}`) is served from the pull-request list instead, and the

A review run that produced no acceptance record (pending or failed
verification, incomplete review, not ready) cannot approve or merge. Attempt-

## One transient GitHub failure no longer ends a step

The `actions/github-script` client defaults to `retries: 0`, so a single HTTP 5xx ended any step that called the API. A
`GET /pulls/{n}` within about a minute of a pull request being opened was observed returning 503 to several runs at once.
Every packaged step of the Clouseau action now installs a read retry first (`src/github-retry.cjs`): GET and HEAD are
retried on 5xx or a short rate limit with the shared 2 s / 6 s / 15 s backoff, while writes keep their own handling, which
checks that an earlier attempt did not land, so a review, comment or merge is never sent twice. A consumer workflow
upgrades by adding `retries: 3` under `with:` of each of its own inline `actions/github-script` steps, which only read.
For the reference template these are the five steps of `assess-intent` and `check-author`.

## Approved PRs after a sibling merge moves the base

Approval, the assessment and any local receipt are bound to the head **and** the
base. When one approved PR merges, every other approved PR is left behind
(GitHub auto-merge just waits) and no gate re-runs, so the
`clouseau-needs-branch-update` notice from the gate can never appear. The base
moves on a merge, so the engine reconciles with the `reconcile-base` operation.
A `push` to the base branch fires only for **human** merges: a merge made by
the bot with `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the whole unattended path) creates no push event,
because GitHub starts no workflow from events caused by `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The
unattended path therefore reconciles from a trigger that does fire: a
`workflow_run` of the review workflow completing, in a **separate workflow
file** (a workflow is never started by its own completion; it must not name
itself). The operation reconciles when that completed `pull_request_target` run
belongs to a PR that is now merged into the base, and unconditionally on a
`schedule` or manual `workflow_dispatch`, which also covers an auto-merge that
completes after the review run ended. It is idempotent and cheap when nothing
is behind:

1. For every open, ready PR that has a current-head GitHub Actions bot approval
   or armed auto-merge, compare its head with the base. A PR that is not
   behind is left alone.
2. Optional `update-token` (an independent credential such as a fine-grained
   PAT or App token, like `repair-token`): the lowest-numbered stale
   same-repository PR is brought up to date with `update-branch`
   (`expected_head_sha`, no force). That push, unlike a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push,
   starts normal verification, a fresh independent review and, where required,
   a fresh local receipt. Only one PR is updated per push so the next sibling
   merge does not invalidate several in-flight re-reviews; the merge of the
   updated PR is itself a push that updates the next one. Under the protected
   `local_review.base_moved: "update"` every stale same-repository PR is
   updated in the same run instead (see below).
3. Every other stale PR (all of them without `update-token`, forks, deleted head
   repositories, conflicts or a refused update) gets one visible
   `clouseau-needs-branch-update` comment, updated in place on later pushes.

Nothing is approved, merged or re-armed by this operation, and a push made with
`GITHUB_TOKEN` is never used because it would leave the new head without
tests, coverage or review evidence. Evidence is never reused across heads.
Limitation: a PR that is still being reviewed when the base moves is not
touched here; its own gate raises the notice when it finishes.

Consumer workflow template (names are the consumer's own). The human-merge trigger stays in the
verification workflow; the unattended trigger is in a separate file, normally the same file as the
verification-completed reassessment above:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (human merges)
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
jobs:
  reconcile-base:
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    permissions: {contents: read, pull-requests: write, issues: write}
    concurrency: {group: clouseau-reconcile-base, cancel-in-progress: false}
    # checkout main and the frozen engine, then:
    #   operation: reconcile-base
    #   update-token: ${{ secrets.BRANCH_UPDATE_TOKEN }}   # optional
```

```yaml
# .github/workflows/clouseau-reassess.yml (bot merges; a different file than the workflow it watches)
# Commenting on a pull request needs BOTH issues: write and pull-requests: write
# (GitHub reports x-accepted-github-permissions: issues=write; pull_requests=write).
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["Palazzo CI"]
    types: [completed]
  schedule: [{cron: '11,41 * * * *'}]    # optional, off the hour so schedules do not align: auto-merges that finish after the review run
jobs:
  reconcile-base:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request_target')
    permissions: {contents: read, pull-requests: write, issues: write}
    concurrency: {group: clouseau-reconcile-base, cancel-in-progress: false}
    # checkout main and the frozen engine, then operation: reconcile-base (same inputs as above)
```

This repository ships exactly this separate file for itself as `.github/workflows/clouseau-reconcile.yml` (watching `Clouseau CI`, no update token), so its own approved PRs also receive the notice after a bot merge.

The reconciler decides its scope from the trigger. A push, a schedule, a dispatch, or the completed review run
of a **merged** PR re-checks every open PR. The completed review run of an **open** PR re-checks only that PR:
in a batch the first merge usually happens while the others are still under review, and the later approvals
have no merge event after them, so without this their notice would never be posted. Notices are idempotent
(one comment per PR and head, edited in place when the base moves again). Every run states what it did, or why
it did nothing, in its log and run summary (`Base reconciliation skipped: ...`, `Base reconciliation (...)`),
and the template's `explain` job writes a summary line even when the `reconcile-base` job is skipped by its
`if:` (the completed run was a `pull_request` run, not a `pull_request_target` review run).

The shared contract test `assertBaseReconciliation` encodes both forms: a push trigger on
the base branch, or a `workflow_run` trigger that watches a different workflow; the push-only or
review-run-only job condition; issues write without contents or actions write; and queued (never
cancelled) runs. A condition that also admits `schedule` is accepted because it still contains the
`workflow_run` clause.

### Opt-in: update the branch instead of holding

A consumer that sets the protected `local_review.base_moved: "update"` (valid only with `binding: "diff"`; the default
`"hold"` is today's behavior; see [local review](local-review.md#base-moved-hold-or-update-opt-in)) lets the gate merge a moved
base into the branch server-side instead of posting the notice when the pull request is approved (including any maintainer confirmation the gate requires), and lets `reconcile-base` update every stale same-repository
PR in one run instead of one at a time. Upgrade steps:

1. Pass `update-token` to the gate step of `approve-and-merge`. The reference template passes
   `update-token: ${{ secrets.CLOUSEAU_REPAIR_TOKEN }}`, the same secret as `repair-token`: one token serves both. Use
   whatever secret your workflow already passes as `repair-token` (this repository's own workflow calls it `DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN`).
2. That token must start workflows (a `GITHUB_TOKEN` push starts none) and needs contents: write on the repository. When the
   base brings changes to `.github/workflows/`, GitHub refuses the update unless the token may also change workflows
   (a fine-grained token or GitHub App with workflows: write, or a classic token with the `workflow` scope). The gate then
   fails with GitHub's refusal and nothing is updated. Grant it, or update such a branch by hand.
3. Set `"base_moved": "update"` under `local_review` in `.github/clouseau.json` (a protected change, confirmed by the owner).

On the updated head only the new head's own `pull_request` run follows: `verify` skips the receipt-covered steps while the
diff-bound receipt still attests, so they are not re-run on the merged base (as with `clouseau refresh` answering `updated`), no
reviewer is asked, and under `confirmation: "diff"` the owner's confirmation carries. The old head's gate ends with cause
`base_update_requested`. Loop bound: an update is requested only for the assessed head with only the base moved, with
`expected_head_sha`; a rerun sees the new head and requests nothing, the new head carries the new base, and updating a
branch never moves the base. Without the setting the token is never used.

On a controller-managed private-owner repository (the merge the acceptance controller performs itself), the update happens at
the gate's first check, before the controller's merge, and the updated head then merges by the same atomic fast-forward. The
base can still move in the seconds between that check and the controller's own re-read of the pull request; that rare case,
and an exact-revert record, keep holding with the notice (fail closed) and are updated by the next reconcile or base move.

## Operations and boundaries

In artifact mode, find `clouseau-engine-<run id>-<attempt>` for the full central
SHA, source and digest. In summary mode, use the resolver's workflow summary;
every engine step also records its identity there. Acceptance records carry the same
engine identity. Keep review, receipt reuse, hosted tests, approval, merge and
deployment as distinct evidence. When CODEOWNERS exists on the protected base,
automatic merge remains restricted to authors
who own every affected path under protected-base CODEOWNERS; other contributors
need code-owner involvement and manual merge. Write access alone grants no
ownership.
Confirmed absence leaves the optional ownership gate inactive; unavailable or
invalid ownership evidence does not. All other acceptance gates remain mandatory.

The resolver's `provenance` input defaults to `artifact`. Repositories without
Actions artifact storage can explicitly select `summary`; this skips only the
additional provenance artifact upload. Resolution, protected-source validation,
immutable checkout, digest computation, SHA/digest outputs, the full workflow
summary and the run-bound engine identity in review records remain mandatory.
Unknown modes fail before resolution. This does not change review-record
transport: use its separately supported `job-output` mode when needed. Neither
mode turns a failed resolution, verification or review into success.

Normal central releases reach the next consumer run without consumer pin or
digest PRs, and the bootstrap itself follows protected main (`@main`), so there is no bootstrap
pin to maintain. A workflow change that adds or moves the reference is still a protected control
change reviewed through an ordinary installation PR.

Palazzo source CI and its separate wiki workflow each freeze their own version;
they do not share a run identity. Colombo's source CI uses this mechanism. Its
older documentation action pins are inside `backend-deploy.yml`, whose changes
trigger production deployment; those remain outside this installation. Deployment
commands, triggers and documentation publication boundaries are unchanged.

## Review evidence transport

Review source inventories use controller-assigned numeric indices over the model
transport. The controller restores each full immutable source ID before the
existing completeness validation. Unknown, duplicated or substituted sources
remain errors; malformed evidence cannot authorize approval.
The report schema permits an inspected dependency only when its current-head
source is supplied. Call-site evidence cannot establish dependency inspection;
missing material source must be requested or explicitly reported missing.



Local qualification can add explicit operator checks with
`--additional-checks FILE`; these run after accepted-base verification and exact
coverage, cannot change its coverage artifacts, and never replace CI checks.
This records the actual consumer workflow tests without application changes or
deployment. Local evidence uses lossless transport presentation, retaining all
source and prior observations while avoiding duplicate literal text. A transport
limit still fails closed with private diagnostics, never a partial approval.
The workflow contract checks every engine checkout and rejects a later checkout
that could overwrite the frozen source before tests or coverage.
